pr_body:
TCP connection supports keep alive msg (RFC1122)

Fixes #34044
pr_comments:
I have done quick test with this PR and civetweb (STM32H7 board). Keepalive is disabled in Civetweb code by checking `__ZEPHYR__` macro, but it can be easily tweaked.

With `CONFIG_NET_TCP_KEEPALIVE` enabled but keepalive disabled in Civetweb's settings I have seen this assert:
```
ASSERTION FAIL [!sys_dnode_is_linked(&to->node)] @ WEST_TOPDIR/zephyr/kernel/timeout.c:93
```

comming from 
```c
int net_tcp_queue_data(struct net_context *context, struct net_pkt *pkt)
...
#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_NET_TCP_KEEPALIVE)
		if ((net_context_get_state(conn->context) & NET_CONTEXT_CONNECTED) &&
			context->options.keepalive) {
			k_work_reschedule_for_queue(
				&tcp_work_q, &conn->keepalive_timer,
				K_SECONDS(conn->keep_idle));
		}
#endif /*CONFIG_NET_TCP_KEEPALIVE */
...
```

With keepalive enabled in civetweb there are EPSR faults in `sys_clock_isr()`
```
[00:00:47.649,000] <err> os: ***** USAGE FAULT *****
[00:00:47.649,000] <err> os:   Illegal use of the EPSR
[00:00:47.649,000] <err> os: r0/a1:  0x24064760  r1/a2:  0x00000000  r2/a3:  0x24013568
[00:00:47.649,000] <err> os: r3/a4:  0x00000000 r12/ip:  0x00000000 r14/lr:  0x9002d079
[00:00:47.649,000] <err> os:  xpsr:  0x6000000f
[00:00:47.649,000] <err> os: s[ 0]:  0x00000000  s[ 1]:  0x00000000  s[ 2]:  0x00000000  s[ 3]:  0x00000000
[00:00:47.649,000] <err> os: s[ 4]:  0x00000000  s[ 5]:  0x00000000  s[ 6]:  0x00000000  s[ 7]:  0x00000000
[00:00:47.649,000] <err> os: s[ 8]:  0x00000000  s[ 9]:  0x00000000  s[10]:  0x00000000  s[11]:  0x00000000
[00:00:47.649,000] <err> os: s[12]:  0x00000000  s[13]:  0xffffffff  s[14]:  0x00000000  s[15]:  0x00000000
[00:00:47.650,000] <err> os: fpscr:  0x12673c0e
[00:00:47.650,000] <err> os: Faulting instruction address (r15/pc): 0x00000000
[00:00:47.650,000] <err> os: >>> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR 0: CPU exception on CPU 0
[00:00:47.650,000] <err> os: Fault during interrupt handling

[00:00:47.650,000] <err> os: Current thread: 0x24013568 (civetweb-worker)
[00:00:47.653,000] <err> os: Halting system
```

Both of these states were triggered just by repeating a download of a single page from civetweb server.

These days are too busy, I will look at this problem the day after tomorrow

issue_context.title: TCP connection does not support keepalive function
issue_context.body: The keepalive function in tcp is very important. When will Zephyr OS support this function?
comments: If the lwip protocol stack is transplanted, the network function of zephyr os will be more powerful.

Indeed, the keepalive messages are currently not there. I cannot really say when they would be implemented. If you want that feature urgently, one option is to send a PR that fixes the issue. As always patches are welcome.

> If the lwip protocol stack is transplanted, the network function of zephyr os will be more powerful.

May I ask why is that more powerful?

For anyone that finds the above fork to implement TCP keepalive on their own -- there is a bug related to disconnects when using keepalive.  The tcp_conn_unref function is missing the lines to optionally cancel the keepalive_timer delayed task as part of its cleanup actions.  Since the memory is zeroed out afterwards, the reference is lost which can then result in "jump to 0" exceptions and hard faults on a disconnect.

Take lines from here:
https://github.com/maweicoltsmart/zephyr/commit/f1c5493faf26b809e4ed258cdae3dfd82bc314c3#diff-9ac8d59b0b68aecce1e4b98cae67d25e5f56a2a53c14316d30850f68f4e6a2f7R551-R553

Then add those lines to here:
https://github.com/maweicoltsmart/zephyr/commit/f1c5493faf26b809e4ed258cdae3dfd82bc314c3#diff-9ac8d59b0b68aecce1e4b98cae67d25e5f56a2a53c14316d30850f68f4e6a2f7R437

I just wonder why #46716 was abandoned as it was quite near for merging. It is rather pointless to have keepalive support patches out-of-tree. @RBartonMesh would you be able to re-submit the patches with the fixes?
ping @RBartonMesh / @maweicoltsmart if possible, please review / try #66316

review_comments:
Please squash the commits together and change the commit message to
```
net: tcp: Add Keepalive support

Implement TCP keepalive support from RFC 1122

Fixes #34044

Signed-off-by: <your id etc>
```
I don't know how to operate it, can you teach me the specific command line code

There are multiple ways, but I usually do all tree manipulations with interactive git rebase.
So something like this:  `git rebase -i HEAD~2`, then mark the latter commit with "s" (which means squash), and mark the first commit with "r" (which means reword and edit the commit msg) and save.

Also, we do not do merge commits in Zephyr so you need to rebase properly. Please, do not close this PR but just force push a new version `git push -f origin <your-branch>`
Is my last commit redundant? How to revoke it?
Would be good to document these new options.
